questions.question: Which of the following best describes a luminous object?
options: An object that absorbs all light that hits it
An object that gives out its own light
An object that only reflects light from another source
An object that bends light passing through it

questions.question: What happens to light rays when they strike an irregular, non-mirror surface?
options: They are completely absorbed and destroyed
They scatter in many different directions
They pass straight through without changing direction
They reflect in a single, perfectly uniform beam

questions.question: Where in the human eye is light detected by a light-sensitive surface?
options: The iris
The lens
The pupil
The retina

questions.question: What is an echo?
options: A sound wave passing through a vacuum
A sound heard again after reflecting off a hard surface
A change in pitch caused by moving away from a source
A sound wave absorbing energy from soft materials

questions.question: Why do soft materials absorb a large amount of sound energy?
options: They reflect sound waves back toward the source
Sound waves transfer energy by making particles in the soft material vibrate
They contain a vacuum that stops sound from moving
Their particles are held so tightly that sound cannot enter

questions.question: How can unwanted noise inside a room be reduced effectively?
options: By using soft materials to absorb the sound
By removing all air from the room
By making the sound wave travel at a higher speed
By replacing smooth walls with thinner metal sheets

questions.question: In light reflection diagrams, what is the imaginary line called that is drawn at 90° to the surface at the point of reflection?
options: The incident ray
The reflected ray
The normal
The focal line

questions.question: If a ray of light hits a flat mirror with an angle of incidence of 35° to the normal, what will the angle of reflection be?
If an object is placed 2 metres in front of a flat mirror, where does its image appear to be located?
options: 1 metre in front of the mirror
2 metres behind the mirror
4 metres behind the mirror
Directly on the mirror surface

questions.question: What does it mean when we say an image in a plane mirror is laterally inverted?
options: It is upside down
It is smaller than the object
Left and right are swapped
It is blurry and out of focus

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes opaque objects?
options: They transmit all light through them easily
They do not transmit light through them
They are completely invisible in daylight
They produce light of their own

questions.question: Which of the following is a key property of how light travels?
options: It travels in curved waves at low speed
It travels in straight lines at an extremely high speed
It requires a solid material to move forward
It slows down drastically as it enters empty space

questions.question: What causes a shadow to form behind an object?
options: Light bending around an object
An object blocking light, creating an unlit area
Sound waves pushing light away from the surface
Light being focused onto a single bright point

questions.question: What is the fundamental cause of all sounds?
options: Heat transfers
Vibrations
Light rays
Magnetic forces

questions.question: What happens to a sound when the amplitude of its vibration increases?
options: The pitch becomes higher
The sound becomes louder
The speed of sound increases
The sound becomes quieter

questions.question: Which characteristic of a sound wave increases as the frequency of vibrations increases?
options: Volume
Amplitude
Pitch
Echo duration

questions.question: How does sound travel through a medium such as air or water?
options: By particles travelling from the source directly to the ear
By vibrations being passed on between adjacent particles
By light energy carrying sound waves
By air particles disappearing and reappearing

questions.question: Why does sound travel faster through liquids than through gases?
options: Liquids are colder than gases
Particles in liquids are closer together so vibrations pass on more easily
Liquids have no particles to block the sound
Sound waves gain amplitude in liquids

questions.question: Why does sound travel fastest through solid materials?
options: Solids have large gaps between their particles
Strong attractive forces mean many particles vibrate when one does
Solids transmit light along with sound
Particles in solids move rapidly from place to place

questions.question: Why is sound unable to travel through a vacuum?
options: There is too much light in a vacuum
There are no particles to carry the vibrations
The gravitational force in a vacuum is too strong
Temperature in a vacuum stops all motion
